To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in the ground state of N = Z nuclei the isoveter pairing is stronger than the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing, and that this difference is more pronounced for heavier nuclei.

the ground state of N = Z nuclei is described by a mixture of quartetting condensate and condensate of isoscalar neutron-proton pairs and that the isovector proton-neutron pairing correlations are dominant over the isoscaler proton-neutron pairing.

(i) The quartetting ansatz is an efficient tool for the description of the isoscalar–isovector pairing correlations of self-conjugate nuclei; (ii) the competition between isovector and proton–neutron isoscalar pairing is studied in the sd, pf and g _{9/2} shells, and it is found that the proton–neutron pair condensation is always present, even though the isovector quartetting prevails for all the nuclei considered
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a formalism for the description of the ground state of self-conjugate nuclei in the presence of both the isovector proton-proton and proton–neutron pairings and the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing.
the study of the proton-neutron pairing correlation in N=Z nuclei.
a new formalism to treat proton–neutron superfluidity in N = Z systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the isovector quartetting and pair condensation are the two main pairing correlations in the N = Z nuclei.
, for the N = Z nuclei studied here, the isovector quartetting prevails over the isospectral proton–neutron pair condensation.
, for N = Z systems, the quartetting is the dominant mechanism of pairing correlation in the ground state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isovector–isovector pairing correlation energy is larger than the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing correlation energy, but the latter can be of the same order of magnitude as the former.

, in the case of N = Z nuclei, the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing is a minor player, while the isovector proton-neutron pairing, which can be described in terms of quartets, is the main source of the pairing correlation energy.
the isovector quartetting is a general feature for self-conjugated systems of fermions, while the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing is a particularity of the nucleonic systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, at variance of the conventional picture, the quartetting is not a mechanism competing with the pair condensation but, rather, a mechanism which can coexist with pair condensation and which is able to describe the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing in N=Z nuclei.
in N = Z systems the proton–neutron isovector pairing is more important than the isoscalar proton-neutron pairing, in contrast to the situation in N ≠ Z nuclei.
the quartetting is a general phenomenon in N = Z systems of valence nucleons, which is not restricted to the sd shell.
